caseStudy.title: Design Token Pipeline
caseStudy.lead: An assessment of an enterprise design system that app teams in many countries build on, and a proposal for an automated token pipeline from Figma to Web, iOS and Android, with accessibility built in and a safe way to rename tokens.

brief.title: The brief
text: The group's design system is the default component library that country teams build their local apps on. Tokens reached iOS and Android in different ways, and there was no web output at all.
The task was to analyse the libraries and propose how tokens could flow automatically from Figma to every platform, without breaking the apps that already depend on them.

contributions.title: What I did
items: Reviewed the iOS and Android implementations through restricted read-only access.
Compared how each platform turns tokens into code, and where they drift.
Designed the token pipeline from Figma to Web, iOS and Android, with CI checks and pull requests into the platform repos.
Defined accessibility rules for components and typed accessibility keys generated from Figma.
Proposed a migration path for renamed tokens, and reviewed the CI/CD setup.

items.title: Clean, modular libraries
items.text: Both platforms use semantic tokens and multi-brand themes.

items.title: Android generates only colours
items.text: Typography, spacing, shapes, elevation and motion are maintained by hand, with numeric names.

items.title: Platforms drift
items.text: iOS uses a different transformation, so parity depends on discipline. There is no web output.

items.title: Renaming breaks apps
items.text: Apps reference tokens directly. A compatibility window with generated aliases and deprecations keeps them working.

items.title: CI/CD
items.text: Workflows pinned to branches instead of tags, iOS tests switched off in lint and test, no PR gating.

items.title: Language-agnostic accessibility
items.text: The library ships typed accessibility keys; apps resolve them to localised strings. Components keep one stable accessibility node.

architecture.title: The proposed pipeline
architecture.text: One source of truth in Git. Every change is validated and arrives on each platform as a reviewable pull request.

team.title: Team
team.text: The assessment team: me on mobile, a web frontend developer, a Figma designer and the agency's Product Owner, working with the client's design and platform specialists.

outcome.title: The result
outcome.text: The client accepted the assessment. Implementation stayed with the client's internal teams.
